contracts.commit_point: The _verify_meta_signature(raw_body, signature) call at whatsapp.py lines 149-154, executed after reading the raw body (line 150) and before payload parsing (lines 156-158) and before svc.ingest (lines 211-225).
contracts.declared_mechanism: _verify_meta_signature(raw_body, signature_header): fail-closed HMAC-SHA256 check of X-Hub-Signature-256 computed with hmac.new keyed by settings.whatsapp_app_secret and compared with hmac.compare_digest; HTTP 500 when the secret is unset, HTTP 400 when the header is missing, HTTP 403 on mismatch; invoked on the raw request body at the top of the POST handler before parsing.
contracts.forbidden_condition: An inbound POST /webhooks/whatsapp request being parsed or ingested when its X-Hub-Signature-256 header is missing, when its HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body does not match the digest computed with settings.whatsapp_app_secret under hmac.compare_digest, or when whatsapp_app_secret is unset (verification must abort with HTTP 500 instead of proceeding).
pending_binding_information: No supplied source links MessageService.ingest (whatsapp.py lines 211-225) to the Kafka inbound topic or to run_support_agent; the Kafka worker source is not supplied, so agent mediation of this guard cannot be established.
Whether inbound Kafka publication occurs inside MessageService.ingest and strictly after signature verification is unverifiable from the supplied views.
Which specific mediation category (direct_tool, agent_lifecycle_hook, agent_generated_input_to_guarded_effect) would apply if a binding is later found is undetermined.
contracts.protected_operation: Processing of inbound WhatsApp Cloud API events at POST /webhooks/whatsapp: raw-body parsing/validation via WhatsAppWebhookPayload.model_validate and message ingestion via MessageService.ingest.
contracts.protected_resource: The WhatsApp webhook intake endpoint (/webhooks/whatsapp) and the inbound message records (and downstream inbound pipeline) it feeds via MessageService.ingest.
contracts.protection_obligation: Merged from reviewer phase-1 and phase-2 wording: POST /webhooks/whatsapp must reject (fail closed, HTTP 400/403) any inbound WhatsApp webhook event whose X-Hub-Signature-256 header is absent or whose HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body does not verify under constant-time comparison keyed by settings.whatsapp_app_secret; verification must be performed on the raw body before the payload is parsed, before any message is ingested to the database, and before any downstream Kafka publication; if whatsapp_app_secret is unset the endpoint must fail closed (HTTP 500) rather than bypass verification.
scope_limits: Covers POST /webhooks/whatsapp only; the GET webhook verification challenge (hub.verify_token comparison, whatsapp.py lines 86-118) is a separate mechanism not covered by this contract.
The whatsapp_rate_limit dependency (line 125) is separate infrastructure policy and is not part of this obligation.

The guard commits at HTTP request admission; the database ingest and any Kafka publication it precedes occur inside MessageService, whose source is not supplied, so downstream ordering is supported only up to the router boundary.

Supplied source contains no binding of this intake guard to an agent tool, agent lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input reaching a guarded effect; it may be ordinary webhook authentication outside the agent-DEC scope, hence agent_mediation is not_established and no agent_entry_binding evidence is cited.
The unset-secret branch yields HTTP 500 (lines 45-53); that is a fail-closed misconfiguration response, not a per-request authentication decision.
